issues.body: Both job- and step-level checks still use assertNotEqual(value, True). A workflow edit such as continue-on-error: ${{ true }} is parsed as a string by PyYAML and therefore passes these assertions while enabling failure swallowing in GitHub Actions. This is materially the same robustness gap reported in round 1; the current ci.yml itself remains correctly gating.
issues.fix_hint: Require each continue-on-error value to be absent or exactly false, for example assertIn(value, (None, False)), at both the job and fmt-step levels.
issues.title: continue-on-error guard still accepts non-boolean enabling forms

verdict.summary: The rustfmt gate remains correctly enabled and the workspace-wide changes are overwhelmingly mechanical formatting; the only behavioral refactor in sparq-acbench preserves the same request/model/oracle ordering. The round-1 robustness finding remains unfixed: the structural test still compares continue-on-error only against boolean True, so expression/string forms that GitHub Actions can interpret as enabling failure swallowing evade the guard. This is a minor test-hardening gap rather than a defect in the checked-in workflow, which has no continue-on-error setting, so approval remains appropriate. Progress is stagnant because the same minor finding remains at the same severity.
